title: Vendor lock-in as a risk with a price, not as a slogan

videos.script: Somebody in every architecture review says the same sentence. We should avoid vendor lock-in. It sounds like prudence, and it decides nothing. {{slogan}} Lock-in is a cost. It is what you would pay to switch, and you can estimate it in hours, like any other piece of work. {{switching}} Then you ask how likely the switch is. A large cost you will almost certainly never pay is worth less than a smaller one you probably will. Multiply the two and you have the expected cost of the lock-in. {{expected}} Avoiding lock-in costs money too. An adapter layer, a second integration, features you give up to stay portable. That is the number to set against the expected cost. {{portability}} Coreto has two lock-ins on the table. A managed database the Catalogue team depends on, and the payment gateway behind checkout. The same arithmetic tells it to accept one and pay to escape the other. By the end of this lesson you can make that call in money, and write down why. {{two}}
